subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally block explicit no-auth non-loopback Gateway service installs during `openclaw gateway install` and update-driven refresh before rewriting the managed service?
rationale: The patch aligns install-time behavior with the existing runtime safety boundary, but it can make existing invalid managed installs fail earlier and leaves broader service-rewrite surfaces out of scope.

options.title: Accept the earlier install block
options.body: Merge the narrowed guard so invalid explicit no-auth non-loopback installs stop before service rewrite with a clearer remediation message.

options.title: Require shared service-rewrite policy
options.body: Ask the author to move or mirror the guard into a shared install policy if every service rewrite path should enforce the same invariant before merge.

options.title: Pause for broader update proof
options.body: Keep this PR paused until maintainers have live proof of the broader update mutation claim and decide whether this narrower fix is enough.

recommendation.title: Accept the earlier install block
recommendation.body: Merge the narrowed guard so invalid explicit no-auth non-loopback installs stop before service rewrite with a clearer remediation message.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for both Gateway auth defaults and managed service install behavior points to steipete.
